Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-08
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 53 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jonas Rivera, Hannah Lee (Redwood) — Dr. Elena Morales, Samir Gupta, Rita Huang, Tom Reeves (Larkspur)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
Redwood gave a hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranker endpoints. Customer is evaluating a search revamp for clinical docs and patient-facing content. Key concerns: latency at 95th, PII handling/data residency, SOC2 / SSO, and cost tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated. Agreed pilot: provide sample corpus + run bench.

Topics covered:
- Hosted embeddings endpoint and vector store flow
- Reranking endpoint (two-stage retrieval + rerank)
- Redwood Console: model selection, quotas, and per-route metrics
- Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching / quantization suggestions)
- Security: encryption, audit logs, SOC2 and VPC/private options

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: okay everyone, thanks for hopping on — hi Elena, hi Samir, hi team. We're going to run through the hosted embeddings plus our reranking endpoint, show the console bits, and then leave time for questions. rough plan 40 minutes demo, 10 for q&a. sound good?
[00:12] Dr. Elena Morales: yeah that's great. we're particularly interested in improving search relevance for clinical notes and patient instructions, also minimizing hallucinations — content safety is huge for us.
[00:22] Jonas Rivera: totally, we'll show a sample pipeline: embed -> vector store -> kNN -> rerank model. the reranker can run as an extra API call that takes your top-N and returns scored candidates.
[00:35] Samir Gupta: quick question on latency — our SLA target is 300ms p95 for query response when the UI is live. is that realistic with hosted?
[00:45] Jonas Rivera: good question. for hosted API, typical median is low, p95 depends on batching and sequence length. with our smart routing and prefix caching we often hit sub-300ms for short queries and cached prefixes; with long context or large top-k it can bump. we can configure a lower-token model variant for latency-sensitive routes.
[01:05] Dr. Elena Morales: by model variant you mean like a quantized smaller model? can you fall back automatically?
[01:12] Hannah Lee: yes — variants are model profiles in the Console. you can set route policies: prefer low-latency variants and fall back to higher-quality if available. that gives predictable SLOs.
[01:25] Rita Huang: what about cost though — switching to a low-latency variant seems like it might raise unit cost?
[01:31] Jonas Rivera: usually lower-latency models are smaller so cost per token is lower; however, if you add an extra rerank call that is another token cost. Redwood Optimize will show cost tradeoffs per-route and recommend batching + caching to reduce units.
[01:45] Tom Reeves: security question — our data is PHI, we need details on data at rest encryption, KMS, and audit logs. also any on-prem options?
[01:55] Maya Patel: definitely — for hosted we offer encryption-at-rest, customer-managed KMS is possible on dedicated/private, and audit logs are available via the Console. for PHI the typical pattern is a private deployment or dedicated pools with VPC peering. we'll share the SOC2 pack and our security whitepaper after this call.
[02:10] Samir Gupta: ok can you walk through a quick live demo of an embeddings -> rerank flow with an example clinical query?
[02:17] Jonas Rivera: yep. i'm going to share my screen. (screen share) starting in the Console — here's the API play to generate embeddings, you POST to /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-v2, you get vector back. next call is to your vector DB for kNN, then we call /v1/rerank with the candidate docs plus query and it returns scores. I'll run an example.
[02:44] [02:44] Jonas Rivera: sample query: "what are common follow-up steps after outpatient knee arthroscopy?" sending to embed...
[02:50] [02:50] (typing sounds)
[02:58] Jonas Rivera: okay embeddings returned — this is quick — now simulating kNN: top16 candidates. now calling rerank endpoint with the query, top16, model=rerank-tuned-1.
[03:12] Jonas Rivera: rerank result — top three: document A (post-op instructions), doc B (recovery timeline), doc C (complication signs). scores include a confidence and alignment note.
[03:24] Dr. Elena Morales: interesting — the ordering looks good. does the reranker truncate or does it use entire doc?
[03:30] Jonas Rivera: typically you send a snippet per candidate — a passage or summary. we support structured payloads so you can pass meta fields and the reranker will use them. also there is an experimental full-doc rerank but that increases latency.
[03:45] Rita Huang: you mentioned structured output — can it return JSON for UI rendering?
[03:49] Hannah Lee: yes — function-style structured outputs or JSON schema enforcement; you can have the reranker output a rationalization string plus a structured reason code which helps for audits.
[04:02] Samir Gupta: in terms of integration, we're using Pinecone today — any issues using your hosted endpoints with external vector DBs?
[04:10] Jonas Rivera: none — most customers do embed with us and store vectors in their DB. we also have native integrations and connector docs. you can also use our hosted vector store if you want a single managed stack.
[04:22] Dr. Elena Morales: how do you handle PII? e.g., patient names that might be in notes — do you recommend client-side redaction?
[04:29] Maya Patel: we recommend token-level redaction/PII scrub before embedding. Redwood does not use customer's content to train models on hosted, and we support enterprise data retention controls — we'll include the retention policy doc.
[04:42] Tom Reeves: can we get an assurance about data residency? some of our data must stay in us-east only.
[04:49] Hannah Lee: yes, region pinning is available for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we can route to a US region by default and discuss contractual commitments for residency for enterprise contracts.
[05:00] [05:00] Dr. Elena Morales: can you show the Console latency/cost metrics?
[05:05] Jonas Rivera: sure — switching to Observability tab — per-route token breakdown, p50/p95 latencies, and cost per token. here's a demo route configured for search: you can see batching set to auto, and prefix cache enabled. Notice the cost slider where Optimize suggested quantization to int8 for that route.
[05:28] Rita Huang: what does Optimize mean by quantization suggestions — is it automatic or a recommendation?
[05:32] Hannah Lee: it's a recommendation — the system analyzes your workload (sequence length distribution, token counts) and suggests an optimal quantization and batching config. you can run an evaluation job that simulates changes and produces a delta in latency & cost.
[05:47] Samir Gupta: for our corpus size (roughly 1.2M docs, average 250 tokens) what's the typical throughput if we run hosted?
[05:55] Jonas Rivera: hosted API handles high throughput but heavy corpuses often move customers to Dedicated for throughput predictability. we'll run capacity modeling for you; as a ballpark, with batching and caching you could expect hundreds of QPS on reserved pools — live hosted varies with multi-tenant load.
[06:12] Dr. Elena Morales: can we do A/B with reranker configs? we'd like to compare existing TF-IDF ranking vs Redwood rerank.
[06:18] Maya Patel: yes — Console supports canary and A/B rollouts per route. you can split traffic and measure metrics in the same UI.
[06:26] Tom Reeves: liability question — if the model returns incorrect medical advice, any thoughts on guardrails?
[06:31] Jonas Rivera: we recommend multi-step defenses: filter candidate set to validated content, add conservative rerank scoring, have human-in-loop flows for high-risk queries, and monitor drift with quality alerts. we also have provenance metadata so you can surface where the answer came from.
[06:50] [06:50] Dr. Elena Morales: sounds good. can you share an example of the audit log format?
[06:54] Hannah Lee: yes — it includes request id, route, model variant, tokens consumed, and a link to stored inputs/outputs depending on retention. we'll attach the schema to the follow-up email.
[07:06] Rita Huang: on pricing, what's the typical pilot structure for a healthcare customer?
[07:11] Maya Patel: pilots are usually time-boxed with usage caps — e.g., 30-day pilot with a reserved credit, API keys scoped to pilot env. we'll include a template quote. if you expect heavy QPS, we might recommend a short Dedicated trial.
[07:25] [07:25] Samir Gupta: for the benchmark you mentioned — can you capture p95 and cost/tok? we want to compare to VectorX numbers.
[07:31] Jonas Rivera: yes, benchmark will include median, p95, cost per query, and the raw results. we'll also show the rerank uplift metric (nDCG or MRR) if you provide labeled queries.
[07:44] Dr. Elena Morales: small thing— are there SDKs for our stack? we're on Go backend and React frontend.
[07:50] Hannah Lee: we have official SDKs for Python, Node, and a Go community SDK. REST endpoints are language agnostic. for React we typically recommend client-side calls to a secure proxy.
[08:00] [08:00] Jonas Rivera: jumping back to demo — i'll show a rerank payload example in the API playground... (reads) {query:..., candidates:[{id:.., snippet:..}], metadata:{site: clinic}} — note: transcription may garble braces in the auto notes but the playground will have the sample.
[08:30] [08:30] Samir Gupta: any gotchas with retries and idempotency? our UI will send retries on timeout.
[08:35] Jonas Rivera: good point — we recommend client-side idempotency keys for generation endpoints; for rerank it's usually idempotent if the same payload is sent, but include idempotency in your request headers if you expect duplicates.
[08:50] Rita Huang: can we pin a model version? regulatory teams want deterministic behavior.
[08:55] Maya Patel: yes you can pin model versions and freeze config; Console shows version history and frozen rollouts.
[09:05] [09:05] Tom Reeves: last security Q— SSO / SAML support? role-based access?
[09:10] Hannah Lee: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC with fine-grained roles. audit events integrate with your SIEM.
[09:20] Dr. Elena Morales: thanks, this has been helpful. next steps recap please?
[09:25] Maya Patel: sure — recap: 1) We'll send pilot pricing, SOC2/security docs, and console screenshots (Maya) by 2027-04-10; 2) Larkspur to send anonymized sample corpus + 200 labeled queries by 2027-04-12; 3) Jonas will run and share a 2k-query benchmark with p95 and cost deltas by 2027-04-15; 4) schedule follow-up to deep dive private/dedicated options week of 2027-04-19.
[09:46] Dr. Elena Morales: perfect. one note — we'll loop in procurement once the pilot pricing looks good.
[09:52] Maya Patel: great — i'll include procurement contacts in the next email. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links.
